full_judgment: 2. Plaintiff FazIur Rahman (now being dead substituted by his sole heirs plaintiffs O.P.1 Zafrullah Siddiqui and O.P.2 Most. Habiba Khatun, his son and widow respectively) instituted Money Suit No. 56/80 on 23-9-80 against Bangladesh (represented by Additional Deputy Commissioner, L.A., Dhaka) and 40 others stating, inter alia, that the land measuring 7 kathas of Plot No. 407 of C.S. Khatian No. 2227 and Plot No. 408 of Khatian No. 2228 of mouza Shahar Dhaka (comprising the Municipal holding Nos. 20 and 21 Bonogram Road, Dhaka) be-longed originally to the C.S. recorded tenants late Prasanna Kumar Sen (Plot No. 407) and late Bir Chand Dhope (plot No. 408). Plot No. 407 measures .0872 while plot No. 408 measures .0868. One Madan Mohan Basak (son of late Brinda Mohan Basak) acquired -/8/-annas share in C.S. Plot No. 407 while the remaining-8/-annas share of C.S. Plot No. 408 was acquired by Radha Ballav Basak, Gopi Ballav Basak, Pran Ballav Basak and Kala Chand Basak (all sons of late Lachman Basak) in equal shares, while Madan Mohan Basak, Radha Ballav Basak, Gopi Ballav Basak, Pran Balav Basak and Kala Chand Basak purchased .309 acre of land out of total land of .0868 of C.S. Plot No. 408 under different registered deeds. Thereafter Gopi Ballav Basak, Pran Ballav Basak and Kala Chand Basak relinquished their right, title and interest in respect of said .309 acre of Plot No.408 by deed of relinquishment dated 24-8-1934. On the death of said Madan Mohan Basak his 7 sons inherited -/8/-annas share and again on the death of late Bholanath Basak his two sons Nandalal Basak and Sakhi Gopal Basak inherited Bholanath's share as sole heirs. Similarly on the death of Radha Ballav Basak, his sons inherited the share of their father. On the death of Gopi Ballav his two sons inherited Gopi Ballav's share. On the death of Gopi Ballav's son Pa-galnath, Pagalnath's only son Gour Chandra inherited Pagalnath's share. On the death of Pran Ballav his 3 sons inherited Pran Ballav's share. Their names were duly recorded in S.A. Khatian in respect of C.S. Plot No. 407; but in respect of C.S. Plot No.408 name of one Khoda Baksh was wrongly re-corded for the entire area of .0868. Ram Hari Basak, Nitya Gopal Basak, Puma Chandra Basak (all sons of late Madan Mohan Basak), Sakhi Gopal Basak (son of late Bholanath Basak), Kala Chandra Basak (son of Lachman Basak,) Tarakanath Basak (son of late Radha Ballav Basak) Radhan Govinda Basak (son of late Gopi Ballav Basak), Brindaban Basak (son of late Pran Ballav Basak), Nanda Lal Basak (son of late Bholanath Basak) and Radha Sham Sham Basak (son of late Radha Ballav Basak) entered into an agreement to sell to the plaintiff all that piece and parcel of land measuring 7 kathas (duly butted and bounded on the north by the land of H. Chand Dhopi, on the east by Brinda Ban Basak, on the south by Nikunja Kamini and Ganga Chandra and on the west by Gour Nitai Shaha Street (now Bonogram Road) and a portion of plot No.408 on which peice and parcel of land stands a portion of Municipal holding No.21, Gour Nitai Shaha Street) in consideration of a total amount of Rs.29,000/- on their behalf and on behalf of other co-sharers under a written agreement dated 20-9-63. The aforesaid property is the subject matter of the present suit. Due to the promulgation of the East Pakistan (Disturbed Persons Rahabilitation) Ordinance, 1964 the necessary requisites for registration of a proper deed of conveyance could not be obtained. An application for permission of execution and registration of proper conveyance in respect of the aforesaid property was filed before the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka by aforesaid Ram Hari Basak and others in Misc. Case No. 490/64, that the Deputy Commissioner duly recommended the case of the plaintiff to the Relief and Rehabilitation Commissioner who directed further inquiry. But by that time the plaintiffs vendors did not come forward to pursue the said application. Thereafter the plaintiff filed an application u/s 6(2) of the said East Pakistan (Disturbed Persons Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1964 before the Member, Board of Revenue for according permission in Permission Case No. 346/66. The Board of Revenue directed the plaintiff to go to the Relief and Rehabilitation Commissioner. The Relief and Rehabilitation Commissioner under his Memo No. 1557(4) dated 6-8-66 did not accord permission for the entire 7 kathas of)and but accorded permission to the plaintiff to the extent of .065 acre only. Permission in respect of 0.35 acre was not given on the ground that they were shares of Indian Nationals and therefore 0.35 acre had become enemy property. Being aggrieved by the said order of the Relief and Rehabilitation Commissioner the plaintiff filed a case u/s 6(2) of the said Disturbed Persons Rehabilitation Ordinance, 1964 for permission to file a suit for Specific Performance of Contract in a proper court making the vendors, the Relief and Rehabilitation Commissioner, the Government of East Pakistan and the Deputy Custodian, Enemy Property, Eden Building, Dhaka as opposite parties challenging the treatment of 0.35 acre as enemy property being illegal. The then Member, Board of Revenue after hearing the parties accorded permission to file a regular suit for Specific Performance of Contract in respect of the suit property by order dated 28-9-66. Thereafter the plaintiff instituted Title Suit No. 291/ 66 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka for Specific Performance of Contract against the vendors making Relief and Rehabilitation Commissioner and the Deputy Custodian as additional parties. The suit was decreed in favour of the plaintiff on 6-8-67. The decree was sealed and signed on 23-12-67; The sale deed was accordingly executed and registered in favour of the plaintiff through Court on 20-3-69 and possession of the suit property was delivered on 20-4-69. At the time of mutation it transpired that by clerical mistake 7 kathas of land was converted into wrong figures of decimal instead of .1173. The clerical mistake done in the plaint of Title Suit No. 291/66 was carried into the decree and the sale deed. The plaintiff did not succeed in getting the decree corrected u/s 152 C.P.C. up to the level of High Court Division and the Appellate Division refused leave on 18-1-78. Thereafter they filed an application in the said Title Suit u/s 153 C.P.C. praying for amendment of the decree by correction of the mistake regarding conversion of 7 kathas of land into acre/ decimals which had occurred in the schedule of the plaint and schedule of the decree. The Subordinate Judge 1st Court, Dhaka allowed the said application u/s 153 C.P.C. and the deed of rectification was duly executed on 1-1-79 and registered on 3-1-79 by the Subordinate Judge, 1st Court in Title Execution Case No.42/78. After having had the actual possession of the said property through the Court, the plaintiff got his name mutated in the Dhaka Municipality and in the Government Acquired Estate and is in possession as absolute owner thereof peacefully and uninterruptedly living therein and developing the said property by construction at huge cost by paying rent, taxes, etc. in his own name continuously till 7-1-75 (later corrected as 18-1-75) One Belayet Hossain (defendant No.6), Khandaker Abdul Awal (defendant No. 5) forcibly entered into the said property on 17-1-75 ousting the members of the family of the plain-tiff therefrom and grabbed all the household effects. To this effect, the plaintiff lodged an FIR in the local police station on that very date i.e. on 17-1-75 and Sutrapur P.S. Case No. 71(1)75 was started u/s 448, etc. of the Penal Code. In the meantime they managed to get allotment of the said property as enemy property suppressing all the facts and with the active collaboration of the staff of the Government (defendant No.1) Enemy Property Case No. 16/75 was started illegally and malafide by the defendants to perpetuate their' illegal occupation. Defendant No.2 the Additional Deputy Commissioner (L.A.) Dhaka on a misconception of law and facts treated .0567 acre of land as enemy property on the ground that in the registered deed being No. 3426 of the year 1969, the plot No. 407 of c.s. Khatain No. 1953 (ka) being absent the plaintiff could not claim the said land measuring .0567 and on that ground the Additional Deputy Commissioner (L.A.) Dhaka treated the said land measuring .0567 as enemy property vested in the Government. Against the said order dated 7-4-76 of the Additional Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka appeal case No. 204/76-V-1 was filed by the plaintiff on 5-5-76 before the Ministry of Land Administration and Land Reforms, Government of Bangladesh but on 12-12-78 appeal was dismissed and the order of the Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka was upheld. In the meantime the plaintiff could get decree in Title Suit No. 291/66 of the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka corrected and amended u/s 153 C.P.C. and got a rectification deed duly executed and registered by the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka in January, 1979. The plaintiff then approached defendant No. 41 Abdul Hye Sarker, the then Additional Deputy Commissioner-in-charge of vested and non-resident property, Dhaka to revise his predecessor's order dated 7-4-76 but he refused to entertain the application on the ground that he has already filed Title Suit No.59/79 in the 1st Court of Subordinate Judge for declaration of the entire property including .0567 ajutangsha. Defendant No. 41 Abdul Hye Sarker, Additional Deputy Commissioner filed the said suit malafide at the instance of other defendants. The property is not enemy property in the eye of law and the defendants arc living in the suit property as trespassers without any lawful authority. Defendant Nos. 5 Khondaker Abdul Awal and defendant No. 6 Belayet Hossain Khan are lessees of the suit property under the Vested Property Authority. The rest of the defendants are persons related to defendant Nos. 5 and 6 and inducted into the suit property by them for their illegal gain and profits. The plaintiff is entitled to get possession of the suit property under the law. The defendants have been keeping the suit property in their illegal possession and use. The plaintiff is entitled to get mesne profits from the defendants for their unauthorised and illegal use and enjoyment and occupation of the suit property. The defendants were and are jointly and severally liable to pay mesne profits to the plaintiffs. The suit property is very valuable and is being used for residential and business purposes. The defendants are depriving the plaintiffs of benefits and profits of the suit land by living there and by running ration shop. The plaintiff reserves the right to sue defendant No.41 Abdul Hye Sarker, the then Additional Deputy Commissioner, Dhaka for damages as he, at the instance of defendant Nos. 5 and 6, caused the said loss to the plaintiff.
